# the contributor audit: reflection selector and unequal dilation identities

Source: `candidate 84f22b883b24046f`.


The two trapezoid overlap polynomials, strict horizontal loss, and
unique maximizer are correct. Its symmetric overlap gives the lower
depth bound, and the downward original cap attains it, so the exact
ordinary normalized depth is five twelfths. Binary-base products retain
only the own-fiber reflection term. The displayed integer-affine
functional isolates that fiber with a finite oblique cap, giving the
claimed exact mixed depth for every n, including n zero.

The unequal-dilation endpoint identity follows pointwise from opposite
signs and counts boundary points twice. Both reconstructed endpoint
sets lie in the original S, and q-dimensional homotheties have exactly
the stated scaling, including q zero. Thus the cap inequality includes
all ambient orientations and positive boundary mass.

For rational weights, the integer equation is equivalent to the stated
residue class relation. Only pairs of maximal-dimensional fibers can
contribute positive q-measure. Convexity at their integer weighted
center forces their affine directions to agree; otherwise that center
fiber would have dimension larger than q. In that common affine space
the scaled convolution has Jacobian `[t(1-t)]^q`. The unscaled alternative
has the different factor recorded in the note. The master identity,
first moment, finite denominator restriction, irrational case, and
factor-three discontinuity all follow with the claimed indexing.

On a single convex fiber the balanced opposite-dilation inequality and
the denominator power inequality make the midpoint certificate best
within this entire family. Thus the product example also defeats that
unequal-weight repair. It is an auxiliary selector obstruction, not an
OC counterexample.
